Read it before changing a scene so your commands use existing ids and coordinates.

ops.title: 장면 고치기(명령 배치)
ops.description: Edit a scene with a validated command batch and write it to disk — the same validator the Studio editor uses, applied atomically (one invalid command rejects the whole batch and nothing is written). The editor and the running game preview reload from disk on their own, so the user sees the result immediately. PREFER THIS over rewriting the .studio.json by hand for placement, visibility, text, color, add/remove/reorder: it keeps ids, bounds and anchors valid and preserves every field it does not know (logic, engine props). Edit files directly only for things the commands cannot express (new script or op code in outputs/game/src/, assets). Commands: {type:'node.update', id, transform?:{x?,y?,w?,h?,anchor?,z?}, props?:{...shallow merge}} · {type:'node.add', node:{id, parent?:'root'|<node id>, type:'sprite'|'rect'|'text'|'model', transform:{x,y,w,h,anchor?,z?}, props?}} · {type:'node.remove', id} (children go too) · {type:'node.reorder', id, direction:'forward'|'backward'} (to the very front/back) · {type:'scene.update', name} · {type:'action.set', name, steps:[{op, ...args, if?:{key, equals|atLeast|not}}]} (sets logic.actions[name]; built-in ops: toggle, setVisible, say, swapAsset, setText, move, set, add, goto, run, plus the project's own from src/main.js) · {type:'action.remove', name} · {type:'asset.set', asset:{id, file (relative to assets/), width, height}} (declare a material in document.assets, same id replaces — then a sprite can name it in props.asset; studio_list_assets has the files and sizes) · {type:'asset.remove', id} (refused while a node uses it). Behaviors: set props.script to a registered script name, {name, ...config}, or a list of them (built-ins: float, spin, pulse, blink, frames, mover; project scripts live in outputs/game/src/scripts/index.js); null removes it. Drawing props: visible, opacity, rotation (degrees), scale, flipX, tint. Coordinates are container pixels; anchor is top-left (default), center or bottom-center; a node with a parent is positioned relative to that parent's top-left. A sprite's props.asset names an entry of document.assets; a 'model' node draws a GLB asset (declare it with asset.set, file ending .glb) fitted into its box, turned by props.yaw / props.pitch (degrees) — the built-in behavior turntable {speed} spins it; props.onClick names a key of logic.actions.

scene.description: Scene id — the file stem of outputs/game/content/<id>.studio.json (letters, digits, - and _). Get the ids from studio_list_scenes.

commands.description: The command batch, applied in order.

nodes.description: Nodes in the scene after the batch.

Use it when the user asks to build, package, export, release or publish the game, after the changes they asked for are in place. Returns the version, directory and zip path.

ops.title: 빌드 올리기
ops.description: Release a build of the game. `target: "local"` (default) publishes it on this Tinysolver Studio's own web address at /play/<project-slug>/ — no setup, the link stays the same across versions, and it is as public as the Studio's server is. `target: "command"` runs the project's `publish.command` from codeg-project.json (e.g. `npx wrangler pages deploy $CODEG_BUILD_DIR --project-name my-game`, `netlify deploy --prod --dir $CODEG_BUILD_DIR`, `butler push $CODEG_BUILD_ZIP user/game:html5`) and returns the URL that command printed; if the manifest has no publish.command the result says so — add one to the manifest (ask the user which host and account) rather than guessing. Publishes the newest build unless `version` is given; call studio_build first when the game changed since the last build. Use when the user asks to publish, release, deploy, ship or share the game.

Call it before generating or placing a material so you use real ids. Each entry also has `check`: findings against its `use` preset ({level: over|warn|info, code, value, limit, message} — e.g. too many triangles, texture or file too big, a transparent-workflow image that came back opaque); the result carries the preset table as `presets`. ops.description: Bring a generated or downloaded file into the project as a material: fetches `url` (http(s) or a base64 data: URL; png/jpg/webp/gif images, glb/gltf models), writes it under assets/ (default assets/generated/images or assets/generated/models), and registers it in assets/manifest.json with `source` — pass what made it (workflow, prompt, seed, from: the material id it was made from) so the material can be traced and remade. When the url is an output of the project's connected generator, the generator's copy is deleted after the import (the project keeps the file). Give `file` instead of `url` to register a file that is already under assets/. Use this after generating with your own image/3D tools (e.g. a genai generate_image / generate_3d result url). ops.title: 재료 생성(genai)
ops.description: Make a new material with the project's connected generator (codeg-project.json `generate.url`, the genai API) and import it with its provenance — the same operations as the Studio material drawer's buttons. Kinds: `image` draws from `prompt` (default workflow qwen-image-21-rgba on the generator's GPU: a transparent PNG; with `from`, that image is the img2img source; `provider` + `model` draw it in the cloud instead — studio_generator_options lists the choices). `edit` redraws the image material `from` by `prompt` (qwen-image-21-edit; background cut away unless `transparent: false`) — e.g. restyle a render keyframe. `tpose` redraws a character image `from` standing in a T-pose (same outfit) — do this BEFORE `3d` for any character that will be rigged: a T-pose rigs cleanly far more often (5/6 vs 1/6 measured). `3d` lifts the image material `from` into a textured GLB (TRELLIS.2; `target_faces` 1000–2000000; `texture_size` 1024|2048|4096). `rig` puts a skeleton and skin weights into the model material `from` (one standing character, SkinTokens) → a rigged GLB; then studio_render `mode: walk` makes it walk. `video` animates the image material `from` as the first frame (MiniMax H3 i2v, ~1.5 min): `prompt` = the motion, the camera move, and a final `Audio: …` line; `duration` seconds (default 5), `width`/`height` (default 768). The shape and colours stay; the motion is drawn by the video model. Usual video path: image → (tpose) → 3d → (rig) → studio_render (turntable or walk) → video from a keyframe still. Takes a minute or more (3D ~2–10 min with a busy queue); the generator machine can be switched off — the result then says so. If no generator is connected the result says how to connect one; ask the user for the address.

from.description: Id of the material fed in: an image (edit · tpose · 3d · video, optional for image) or a 3D model (rig).

prompt.description: image: what to draw · edit: what to change · tpose: an optional note (e.g. 'keep the cape') · video: motion + camera + 'Audio: …'.

workflow.description: Generator workflow name (comfyui — the generator's own GPU). Defaults: qwen-image-21-rgba (image), qwen-image-21-edit (edit · tpose), trellis2 (3d), minimax-h3-i2v (video). studio_generator_options lists what the generator has.

provider.description: image only — who draws it. comfyui (default): the generator's own GPU, free, pick a `workflow`. codex: gpt-image-2 on the generator owner's ChatGPT subscription (~2 min a picture, one at a time). openrouter / openai: metered cloud, pick a `model` (e.g. openrouter google/gemini-nano-banana-2.1 ≈ $0.034 · ~11 s). Cloud pictures come back opaque — fine for a 3D lift, which cuts its own background.

model.description: Cloud model id for provider openrouter / openai (codex needs none), e.g. google/gemini-nano-banana-2.1, google/gemini-3-pro-image. studio_generator_options lists the offered ones with time and price.

seed.description: Default: random, recorded on the material.

width.description: video: canvas width. Default 768 (reshaped to the image's aspect).

transparent.description: edit · tpose: cut the background away. Default true.

use.description: Where it will be used — one of mobile-prop (300–1.5k tris), mobile-character (3k–10k), roblox-meshpart (≤10k recommended, 21k cap), web-ar (30k–50k, texture ≤2048, ≤5MB), pc-hero (20k–100k), print-3d (100k+, closed mesh). studio_list_assets returns the full table as `presets` and judges each material against its `use` in `check`. For 3d it sets target_faces and texture_size unless you give them, and is recorded on the material.

asset.description: One entry of assets/manifest.json: id, file (relative to assets/), kind, bytes, width/height, source (provenance), use, bones?

remote_deleted.description: The generator's copy was deleted after the import.

ops.title: 모델 렌더(Blender)
ops.description: Render a 3D model material with Blender on the user's computer (headless, no window) — the same operation as the Render button on a model in the Studio's material drawer. `mode: "turntable"` (default) circles the camera once around the model and saves a video (H.264 mp4, 24 fps) plus stills at `keyframes`; `mode: "still"` saves one picture. `mode: "walk"` makes a rigged model (one with `bones` in studio_list_assets — rig it with studio_generate_asset kind rig) take a procedural in-place stride, three-quarter view, video + stills. The model is scaled to height 2 and stood on a light ground plate with soft studio lights. Results are registered as materials under assets/generated/renders/ (the video `kind: video`, each still `kind: image`) with their provenance. A still is the usual first frame for a generated video. Takes ~10 s–2 min. If Blender is not installed the result says how to install it or point codeg-project.json `render.blender` at it — tell the user; do not install it yourself.

from.description: Id of a 3D model material (GLB) from studio_list_assets.

cam_dist.description: Camera distance; the model is 2 tall. Default 6.2 (whole body with margin); ~4 frames it tighter.

yaw.description: Where the camera starts, degrees around the model (0 = front).

id.description: Id for the new materials (stills get -fNNN).

ops.title: 촬영장 목록
ops.description: List the film sets of this content project (outputs/film/sets/*.set.json): id, name, duration, how many props and actors, camera ids. A film set is the 3D stage a shot is filmed on — floor, lights, props, actors (rigged models with motion), cameras with paths — that the Studio's 3D set view, these tools and the Blender render share.

note.description: A hint for the caller; empty when there is nothing to say.

ops.title: 촬영장 읽기
ops.description: Return one film set as JSON plus `issues` (things that do not break the file but would spoil a render: missing materials, a walking actor without bones, keys after the duration, no camera) and `models` (material id → file under assets/). Fields: fps, duration, frame {width,height} (output size — 720×1280 is a 9:16 short), stage {floor {size,color}|null, background, ambient}, props [{id, asset, position, rotation, height?, scale?}], actors [{id, asset, position, rotation, height?, motion: still|walk, ease, keys?: [{t, position, yaw?}]}], lights [{id, type: sun|point|spot|area, position, target, color, power (sun ≈1–5, others watts), size?}], cameras [{id, name?, lens (mm on a 36 mm sensor, long side), ease, keys: [{t, position, target, roll?}]}]. Space: metres, Y up, right-handed (the glTF convention), front is +Z; rotation is XYZ Euler degrees; a model stands with the middle of its footprint at `position`, `height` scales it to that many metres tall. Time: seconds 0–duration; cameras and moving actors carry `keys`, blended per segment with `ease` (smooth = u²(3−2u), default · linear), the first key holds before it and the last after it. Read it before changing a set so your commands use existing ids.

set.description: Set id — the file stem of outputs/film/sets/<id>.set.json (letters, digits, - and _). Get the ids from studio_list_sets.

path.description: Project-relative path of the set file.

models.description: Material id → model file under assets/.

ops.title: 촬영장 만들기
ops.description: Create a film set outputs/film/sets/<set>.set.json with a starter stage: a 30 m floor, three area lights (key, fill, rim), one camera `cam_a` 6 m in front looking at the middle, 15 s at 24 fps, 720×1280 (writes outputs/film/sets/README.md with the schema the first time). Refuses an existing id. Then add props and actors (3D model materials from studio_list_assets) and cameras with studio_apply_set_commands.

ops.title: 촬영장 고치기(명령 배치)
ops.description: Edit a film set with a validated command batch and write it to disk — the same operation the Studio's 3D set view runs when the user drags something, applied atomically (one invalid command rejects the whole batch and nothing is written). The view reloads from disk on its own. PREFER THIS over rewriting the .set.json by hand: it keeps ids unique, numbers in range, keys sorted, and preserves every field it does not know. The result carries the new file and its `issues` — fix them. Commands: {type:'set.update', name?, fps?, duration?, frame?:{width,height}, stage?:{floor?, background?, ambient?}} (frame and stage merge) · {type:'add', kind:'prop'|'actor'|'light'|'camera', item:{id, ...}} (ids are unique across all four kinds; a camera needs keys:[{t, position, target}]) · {type:'update', id, patch:{...}} (shallow merge; null clears a field such as height) · {type:'remove', id} · {type:'key.set', id, key:{t, position?, target?, yaw?, roll?}} (a camera's or actor's key at t — merged into the key already at that time, else added; a new camera key needs position and target) · {type:'key.remove', id, t}. Space: metres, Y up, right-handed (the glTF convention), front is +Z; rotation is XYZ Euler degrees; a model stands with the middle of its footprint at `position`, `height` scales it to that many metres tall. Time: seconds 0–duration; cameras and moving actors carry `keys`, blended per segment with `ease` (smooth = u²(3−2u), default · linear), the first key holds before it and the last after it.

set.description: Set id — the file stem of outputs/film/sets/<id>.set.json (letters, digits, - and _). Get the ids from studio_list_sets.

path.description: Project-relative path of the set file.

models.description: Material id → model file under assets/.

ops.title: 촬영장 찍기(Blender)
ops.description: Film one camera of a film set with Blender on the user's computer (headless): the set document becomes a Blender scene as written — floor, lights, each prop and actor model placed and sized, walking actors taking a procedural stride while their keys move them, the camera following its keys — and the span from..to is rendered as a video (H.264 mp4 at the set's fps) plus stills at `stills` (seconds). Results are registered as materials under assets/generated/renders/ (`<set>-<camera>` by default; stills get -fNNN) with their provenance (source.from `set:<id>`, camera, span). Missing model files draw as boxes and come back in `warnings`. A still is the usual first frame for a generated video (studio_generate_asset kind video). Takes ~10 s–a few minutes. If Blender is not installed the result says how to install it — tell the user; do not install it yourself.

ops.title: 모델 1번 호출(claude · codex)
ops.description: Ask a model once and get JSON back in the shape you give. Runs the machine's own `claude` (`claude -p`) or `codex` (`codex exec`) CLI on the owner's subscription — no API key — with no tools except reading the attached pictures, no session kept, and the user's hooks and MCP servers left out. `schema` is the JSON Schema the answer must have (an object schema; for codex keep it strict: every property in `required`, `additionalProperties: false`). The answer is checked against it again here: `ok: false` with a note (and the answer it got as `output`) when it does not fit. Use it for one-shot judgements — describe or score a picture, pull fields out of text — not for work that needs tools or several turns. Takes ~10 s–2 min. If a CLI is missing or logged out the note says so — tell the user; do not log in yourself.

prompt.description: What to ask. The attached pictures are listed after it.

images.description: Picture files to attach — absolute, or relative to the project (e.g. assets/generated/x.png).

schema.description: JSON Schema of the answer, with "type": "object".

model.description: The CLI's model name (claude: sonnet · opus · haiku …; codex: gpt-5.5 …). Default: the CLI's own.

timeout_secs.description: Seconds before the call is stopped. Default 300.

model.description: The model that answered (claude reports it; codex: the one asked for, else null).

cost_usd.description: claude's reported cost; null for codex.

usage.description: Token counts as the CLI reports them: claude's usage object, codex's { total_tokens }.

ops.title: 흐름 목록
ops.description: List the flows of the Tinysolver Studio content project: flows/<id>.flow.json — documents that wire Studio parts (ops), model calls and human checks into one job (sequence, parallel, each-item fan-out, if, repeat). Each with its id, title, the `want` line, its input names, node count and `issues` (a flow with issues can't run). Read-only.

items.description: { id, title, want, inputs[], nodes, issues[] }

ops.title: 흐름 읽기
ops.description: Read one flow document with its problems (`issues`). Read it before changing a flow or starting a run so you use its real input names. Read-only.

flow.description: A flow document: { schema: 1, id, title?, want: { text, good[], bad[] }, inputs: { name: default }, steps: [node], output? }. Node: { id, kind, note?, keep_going? } plus by kind — op: { op, args } · model: { op? (default model_once), args } · human: { ask, show (items on the card), pick: one|many|text|ok } · flow: { flow, inputs } · set: { value } · seq: { steps } · parallel: { branches: [[node]] } · each: { over: list or { name: list } (their product), as?, steps, limit? } · if: { when, then, else } · repeat: { max, until?, steps } · agent (L4, not yet). Arguments reach earlier results with ${...}: ${inputs.x}, ${node.output.field}, ${each_node.*.inner.path}; inside each the bound names and ${index}; inside repeat ${round} and ${prev}. A condition is { left, op: eq|ne|gt|gte|lt|lte|exists|truthy|falsy|in, right } or { all: [..] } · { any: [..] } · { not: .. }.

ops.title: 흐름 쓰기
ops.description: Write a flow document to flows/<id>.flow.json (creates or replaces it). It is checked first and refused with its `issues` if it could not run (unique node ids, a `want` line, known kinds). Start every flow with `want`: what is wanted in one line, with good and bad examples — runs are judged against it.

flow.description: A flow document: { schema: 1, id, title?, want: { text, good[], bad[] }, inputs: { name: default }, steps: [node], output? }. Node: { id, kind, note?, keep_going? } plus by kind — op: { op, args } · model: { op? (default model_once), args } · human: { ask, show (items on the card), pick: one|many|text|ok } · flow: { flow, inputs } · set: { value } · seq: { steps } · parallel: { branches: [[node]] } · each: { over: list or { name: list } (their product), as?, steps, limit? } · if: { when, then, else } · repeat: { max, until?, steps } · agent (L4, not yet). Arguments reach earlier results with ${...}: ${inputs.x}, ${node.output.field}, ${each_node.*.inner.path}; inside each the bound names and ${index}; inside repeat ${round} and ${prev}. A condition is { left, op: eq|ne|gt|gte|lt|lte|exists|truthy|falsy|in, right } or { all: [..] } · { any: [..] } · { not: .. }.

ops.title: 흐름 돌리기
ops.description: Run a flow. Every node's input, output, who answered, time and cost are recorded in runs/<flow>/<run>/run.json. A `human` node stops the run with a card (card_list, run_answer). Without `wait` it runs in the background — follow it with run_get. Generation and model nodes cost time and money: say what the run will do before starting a big one.

from_run.description: An earlier run of this flow to start from: every node whose definition and input are unchanged reuses that run's output (no new call, no new cost), and its answered cards stay answered while they ask the same. Change one node, run from the last run, then run_compare the two.

label.description: A line on what this run tries differently.

wait.description: Wait until it finishes or stops at a human card. Default false: answer at once with the run id and run in the background.

items.description: { key, ask, show, pick: one|many|text|ok, since }

ops.title: 실행 목록
ops.description: List flow runs, newest first, with status (running · waiting · done · failed), cost, time and any card they wait on. Read-only.

flow.description: Only this flow's runs. Omit for all.

items.description: { flow, run, status, label, want, from_run, started_at, ended_at, ms, cost_usd, nodes, waiting: [{ key, ask }], note }

ops.title: 실행 기록 읽기
ops.description: Read one run's record: the flow as it was, the inputs, and per node what went in, what came out, who answered (op, claude/model, human), how long and what it cost, plus the cards it waits on. Read-only.

run.description: runs/<flow>/<run>/run.json: { id, flow, status: running|waiting|done|failed, want, inputs, flow_doc, from_run?, label?, started_at, ended_at?, ms, cost_usd, nodes: [{ key, node, kind, status, input, output, who, started_at, ms, cost_usd?, log[], note?, reused_from? }], waiting: [card], answers, output, note? }. A node key tells copies apart: gens[2].img (third item of each `gens`), loop#1.x (second round), sub>x (inside flow node `sub`).

ops.title: 카드에 답하기
ops.description: Answer a card a run is waiting on — the person's pick, never your own guess: ask the user, show them the card's items, and pass what they chose. The run then goes on from where it stopped; finished nodes are not called again.

answer.description: pick one: the item's index (0-based) or { index, note } · many: [indexes] or { indexes, note } · text: "…" or { text } · ok: true/false or { ok, note }. `note` (why) is kept with the answer.

wait.description: Wait until the run finishes or stops again. Default false.

items.description: { key, ask, show, pick: one|many|text|ok, since }

ops.title: 실행 둘 나란히
ops.description: Two runs of one flow side by side, node by node: which nodes the flow changed between them, which inputs changed, and both outputs — the 'want → try → what changed → result' trail. Read-only.

items.description: { key, node, flow_changed, input_changed, output_changed, a: side?, b: side? } — side = { status, input, output, who, ms, cost_usd, note, reused_from }

ops.title: 기다리는 카드
ops.description: Every human card a run is waiting on in this project — what to ask the user. Show `ask` and the `show` items (pictures are project-relative paths), then pass their pick to run_answer. Read-only.

items.description: { flow, run, want, card: { key, ask, show, pick, since } }

ops.title: 그림체 카드 저장
ops.description: Write a picked picture style into the project's bible as a card (bible/styles/<slug>.md, pictures copied under assets/styles/<slug>/): name, pictures, prompt, model, why it was picked, the materials and scores, and the run it came from. A card written by hand is never overwritten.

prompt.description: The prompt or condition that made it.

model.description: Model or workflow that made it.

why.description: Why it was picked, in the picker's words.

ops.title: model-pick 판으로 내보내기
ops.description: Export one finished flow run (runs/<flow>/<run>/run.json) as a model-pick comparison round: rounds/<KST date>-<id>/round.json (shape model-pick-round/2) plus media/ in the model-pick checkout. Results are the run's generated pictures (model from each material's source, mapped to model-pick models.json ids), one input per prompt labelled by its condition, the scoring node's scores and the owner's pick. The round is always internal (dev only — the owner decides on making anything public) and says every output is AI-made; a codex line is the owner's personal subscription and is flagged never to go public. A task not in model-pick tasks.json or a model not in models.json stops the export with a note — add it there first (in the model-pick repo), or map a name with `models`. With check: true it runs model-pick tool/publish.sh --dry-run. It does not publish: the caller commits the round in the model-pick repo and runs tool/publish.sh on the LAN (Vault). Refuses a run that is still running.

id.description: Round id after the date. Default <flow>-<run without its date>.

task.description: model-pick task id. Default the flow's task, else text-to-image.

models.description: Run model names → model-pick models.json ids, for names that differ.

overwrite.description: Replace an existing round folder of the same id.

personal_subscription.description: A codex (owner's personal subscription) line is in the round.
